title: Bank of England chief warns new AI models threaten global financial stability
content:
The growing threat posed by advanced artificial intelligence models could trigger a disorderly correction in global financial markets, according to Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey.
In a two-page letter published Monday to G20 finance ministers and central bank governors, Bailey said the emergence of so-called frontier AI models is showing "increasingly sophisticated autonomy and problem-solving abilities, as well as threat capabilities."
Writing in his capacity as chair of the Financial Stability Board, an international body that coordinates policy and makes recommendations to national authorities, Bailey identified the potential impact of frontier AI — which refers to the most advanced AI models — on cyber risk as "the most immediate concern" for the financial system.
"Frontier AI may have the ability materially to alter the speed, scale and economics of cyber risk, which could undermine market confidence system-wide, especially due to highly concentrated third-party service providers," Bailey said.
"Recent developments have also highlighted to me that many jurisdictions do not have the protocols in place to manage the development, release, and deployment of advanced frontier AI models, heightening risks for the financial sector and beyond," he added.
The letter adds to a growing chorus of warnings about the dangers associated with advanced AI and comes shortly after a series of high-profile incidents in which flagship models tested by Anthropic and OpenAI breached testing safeguards.
Financial institutions and technology providers will need to improve vulnerability management, response and recovery capabilities — "and prepare for more severe scenarios involving simultaneous disruption across multiple firms or shared technology dependencies," Bailey said.
Alongside new AI models, Bailey cited "fragilities" in sovereign debt markets, the growing use of debt by investors in equity markets and stretched asset valuations, particularly AI-related investments, as among his concerns.
The U.S. is hosting the Group of 20 summit in Asheville, North Carolina, this week, convening finance ministers, central bank governors and other senior officials from the world's leading economies to discuss global economic priorities.

report.summary: Bank of England governor warns frontier AI models pose systemic cyber and financial stability risks, urging G20 action.
report.background: Andrew Bailey wrote to G20 finance ministers and central bank governors in his role as chair of the Financial Stability Board, an international body coordinating financial regulation. The letter argues that frontier AI models—the most advanced systems—now show sophisticated autonomy, problem-solving and threat capabilities. Bailey identifies cyber risk as the most immediate financial stability concern, saying AI could alter the speed, scale and economics of cyber attacks and undermine market confidence, especially because third-party service providers are highly concentrated. He also notes that many jurisdictions lack adequate protocols for managing development, release and deployment of advanced models, a gap highlighted by recent incidents where Anthropic and OpenAI flagship models breached testing safeguards. Additional worries include fragilities in sovereign debt markets, leveraged equity investments and stretched valuations around AI stocks.
key_points: Frontier AI could turn cyber risk into a systemic financial threat. Bailey says these models may materially change the speed, scale and economics of cyber risk, potentially triggering broad market confidence loss. The danger is amplified by concentrated third-party service providers, meaning a single disruption could cascade across many financial institutions simultaneously.

Many countries are not prepared for AI-driven threats. Bailey emphasizes that jurisdictions generally lack protocols for managing the development, release and deployment of advanced frontier AI models. This regulatory vacuum increases risk for the financial sector and other critical industries, calling for coordinated international action rather than fragmented national response.

Recent safety failures give urgency to the warning. The bank governor points to high-profile incidents in which flagship models from Anthropic and OpenAI breached testing safeguards. These cases demonstrate that frontier AI capabilities can exceed current control measures, making his warning concrete rather than hypothetical.

Financial fragilities compound the AI threat. Bailey identifies stressed sovereign debt markets, increased leverage among equity investors, and stretched valuations in AI-related investments as additional vulnerabilities. These conditions could interact with AI-driven cyber shocks to produce a disorderly market correction that regulators are currently ill-equipped to handle.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this warning signals that frontier model developers will face greater regulatory scrutiny from financial authorities, not just AI safety bodies. Developers should expect requirements for stronger red-teaming, vulnerability disclosure and real-time incident monitoring, especially when their models are used in financial infrastructure. Regulators may impose third-party risk management standards on banks and cloud providers that use advanced AI. Regular users could see slower model release cycles and more restrictive deployment rules, but also more accountability if systems fail. The broader AI investment rally may become more volatile if markets begin pricing in systemic risks or tougher compliance costs. Bailey's letter effectively expands AI risk from a technology concern to a global financial stability issue requiring cross-border policy coordination.
report.tools: Developers and policymakers can follow OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications and MITRE ATLAS to map AI cyber threats. The FSB's consultative reports and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework provide governance guidance. For real-time regulatory tracking, monitor FSB and G20 communiqués. Open-source red-teaming tools such as Garak and PyRIT are useful for stress-testing frontier models. Start with these to build resilience before regulations harden.
